people.name: Prannoy Roy
people.role: Psephologist and journalist, a founder of NDTV, who now presents DeKoder.
people.intro: In a seven-minute episode on 8 October 2026 he sets West Bengal's deletions beside the swing against the TMC, and sets the deletions of women and of Muslim electors beside their shares of the roll. The quotations are from YouTube's English captions, with one word corrected where the captions misheard it.

pieces.title: More SIR Deletions, Bigger BJP Swing? Prannoy Roy DeKodes the Data | DeKoder

claims.quote: In the 25 constituencies with the highest SIR deletion rates, the TMC had a swing against it of nearly 10.5% ... in the 25 constituency with the lowest SIR deletions, the swing against the TMC was down to only 5.3% ... [SIR] deletions almost doubled the swing against the TMC.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: He does not name the data behind the two swing figures. The comparison sets the 25 seats with the most deletions against the 25 with the fewest, with nothing to allow for other ways those seats differ, and the episode does not define the deletion rate.
claims.site: West Bengal's own figures show why other differences matter. Measured by the fall in the roll, the most affected districts are Kolkata North at 27.98 per 100 and Kolkata South at 24.54, and the least affected is Purbo Medinipur at 1.64. By seat the range runs from 39.74 in Chowrangee to 0.34 in Patashpur, so the seats at either end sit in different parts of the state with different histories of voting. In Bihar, the one state where the site has fitted a model of the swing, leaving out each seat's lead at the previous election turns a slope of +0.31 into -0.83.
claims.stops: The site has not fitted a swing model for West Bengal. A vote count also cannot show whether the removals moved votes from one party to another.

claims.quote: women deletions accounted for 62% of all deleted names compared with only 38% of men voters deleted.
claims.rests: The figure matches the Sabar Institute's count as BehanBox reported it, 61.8 per cent. That count takes names deleted and names held for adjudication together.
claims.site: The Chief Electoral Officer's own counts give smaller shares. Women were 53.5 per cent of the 58.2 lakh names left off the draft, against 49.2 per cent of the roll, and 52.6 per cent of the fall from the 2024 roll to the roll at the 2026 nominations. They were over-represented in 21 of 24 districts.
claims.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no split by sex of the adjudication outcomes, so the site cannot check the larger figure.

claims.quote: In other words, the SIR deletion process clearly targeted Muslim voters ... Muslim voter deletions were at a 52% higher deletion rate than non-Muslims.
claims.rests: He does not say how the religion of deleted electors was found. It can only be guessed from names, as the Sabar Institute did. His rate comparison is consistent with his own figures, 30 lakh against 19.8 lakh. The word targeted is a claim about purpose drawn from a pattern.
claims.site: The site does not classify West Bengal's removals by religion. In Bihar, where it does, the religion of the removed is guessed from names and given as a range, because some names cannot be classified. The census share falls inside that range in 18 of 38 districts and below it in 20.
claims.stops: Names give only a guess at religion, and the lists record no purpose. The site makes no claim about what anyone intended.

claims.quote: there's no doubt and there never has been any doubt that election [rolls] need to be constantly updated and cleaned up

strongest: The draft-stage removal rates he gives for Delhi, Maharashtra and Karnataka, about 33, 21 and 20 per cent, are right as reported.
He asks the Commission to explain the gaps by sex and by religion, and the site lacks that data too.
further: Saying the deletions almost doubled the swing reads a cause into a raw comparison of two groups of seats.
Saying the process clearly targeted Muslim voters asserts a purpose that the figures cannot show.
He says the millions removed will now be unable to vote, which leaves out the names put back through Form 6 and appeals.

people.name: The Indian Express
people.role: National daily. The investigation is by Ritika Chopra, its Resident Editor in Mumbai, and the paper later released its special issue free.
people.intro: On 23 September 2026 the paper reported that two Election Commissioners had objected on record to steps taken in the Commission's name. The account rests on documents the paper holds, and it keeps the failures of process apart from the election result.

pieces.title: 14 times in 10 months, two Election Commissioners objected on record to poll panel steps
'Differing views' part of 'decision-making', says EC, does not address concerns two ECs red-flagged

claims.quote: Sandhu and Joshi have formally objected, on record, at least 14 times over the last 10 months – four times on a single day – to decisions taken and orders issued, they say, without their knowledge.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: Documents the paper holds and the site has not seen. The Commission's reply spoke of written notes and differing views and did not deny that the notes exist.
claims.site: The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists each dated objection with the special issue's page number, and gives the paper's count of 14 in its text.
claims.stops: The site has seen only the paper's account of the notes.

claims.quote: On May 16, Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded on file that the form 'cannot be altered without making amendments in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960' ... Sandhu concurred on May 19. In July, the SIR declaration appeared on the online form anyway.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: The Form 6 declaration itself can be seen on the online form, and the paper reported it on 12 July 2026. The file notes are the paper's.
claims.site: The section on Form 6 on the process page sets out the declaration and the objections to it.
claims.stops: No count exists of the applications the declaration held up.

claims.quote: Of the 294 seats that went to polls, in 49, the SIR deletions exceeded the victory margin. But in these, the spoils were almost evenly shared — 26 were won by BJP and 21 by TMC.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: The paper does not say which measure of deletions it used. Its figures match Newslaundry's third test, which used the deletions under adjudication from the Sabar Institute's data. In the line before, the paper says there was no evidence of the revision's role in the outcome.
claims.site: The Chief Electoral Officer published no removals below the state, so the site measures the fall in the roll from 2024 instead. On that measure the fall exceeds the 2026 margin in 139 of 294 seats. Seats the AITC won lost 12.38 per 100 and seats the BJP won lost 9.41, and set against their own districts the gap shrinks to 0.23 against 0.03.
claims.stops: A fall larger than the margin shows that it could have decided the seat. It cannot show that it did.

claims.quote: the manner in which names were struck off prompted the Supreme Court, in February 2026, to take the last leg of the SIR out of the Commission's hands and get judicial officers to decide on the plight of 60 lakh voters flagged for "logical discrepancies." Of these, 27 lakh electors were subsequently deleted by the Commission.
claims.rests: The totals match the official figures as reported.
claims.site: In West Bengal 60,06,675 names were held for adjudication and 27,16,393 were found not eligible. Of the appeals, 16,10,311, or 49.3 per cent, were against a name's inclusion.
claims.stops: Who filed the 16 lakh appeals against inclusion is not public. The paper says the Commission did not say.

claims.quote: Goa's EROs heard these cases. On the documents produced, they found 97 voters eligible for the final roll. The software had no way to record that decision.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: Documents as the paper reports them.
claims.site: The process page carries the Goa sequence from the special issue, marked as press. Goa left 1,00,042 names off its draft, 8.44 for every 100 electors.
claims.stops: The 97 are the paper's count, and the site holds no list of them.

strongest: It rests on dated documents. It put questions to the Commission and printed the Commission's later press note in full.
It keeps the failures of process apart from the election result in so many words.
further: Very little. Its description of the disquiet as unprecedented in scale and significance is a judgement, and the paper presents it as its own.

people.name: Ravish Kumar
people.role: Journalist and broadcaster, formerly of NDTV India, who publishes daily commentary in Hindi on his own YouTube channel.
people.intro: His episodes of 23 September and 1 October 2026 follow the Express investigation closely. The quotations are from YouTube's Hindi captions and the translations are the site's. Where he relays a party leader's figures, the panel says whose they are.

pieces.title: खुल गई पोल, सामने आ गया खेल, एक्सप्रेस की रिपोर्ट से मचा तहलका
pieces.title_en: The truth is out, the game exposed: the Express report causes an uproar

pieces.title: मुस्लिम वोटर का नाम कौन कटवा रहा है, FORM-7 के पीछे गिरोह?  FORM-6 पर राहुल के सवाल पर EC चुप क्यों?
pieces.title_en: Who is getting Muslim voters' names struck off, a gang behind Form 7? Why is the EC silent on Rahul's question about Form 6?

claims.quote: 10 महीने में 14 बार दो-दो चुनाव आयुक्तों ने मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त से असहमति जाहिर की है।
claims.translation: In 10 months, two Election Commissioners have expressed disagreement with the Chief Election Commissioner 14 times.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: The count of 14 matches the Express. The paper describes them as objections to decisions taken and orders issued without the two Commissioners' knowledge, which is narrower than disagreement with the Chief Election Commissioner.
claims.site: The section Inside the Commission on the process page lists each dated objection with the special issue's page number, and gives the paper's count of 14 in its text.
claims.stops: The site has seen only the paper's account of the notes.

claims.quote: वोट चोरी का सिस्टम पकड़ा गया है। यह सिस्टम कहीं और नहीं चुनाव आयोग के भीतर पकड़ा गया है।
claims.translation: The system of vote theft has been caught. It has been caught nowhere else but inside the Election Commission.
claims.rests: The Express reports objections about process, about access to the roll software, Form 6 and appeals. It reports no theft of votes, and on West Bengal it says there was no evidence of the revision's role in the outcome.
claims.site: Nothing on the site measures purpose.
claims.stops: The lists cannot show what anyone intended, and the site does not say whether anything was stolen.

claims.quote: 97 लोगों ने साबित कर दिया कि वोटर लिस्ट में उनका नाम होना चाहिए ... जिस अधिकारी के सामने दावा किया वो मान भी गया लेकिन दिल्ली से कंट्रोल हो रहा सॉफ्टवेयर उनका नाम वोटर लिस्ट में नहीं जोड़ता है।
claims.translation: 97 people proved they should be on the roll ... the officer accepted their claim, but the software controlled from Delhi did not add them.
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: This matches the Express account of Goa.
claims.site: The process page carries the Goa sequence from the special issue, marked as press. Goa left 1,00,042 names off its draft, 8.44 for every 100 electors.
claims.stops: The 97 are the paper's count, and the site holds no list of them.

claims.quote: मीडिया ने भी 13 करोड़ लोगों का चेहरा गायब कर दिया।
claims.translation: The media too made the faces of 13 crore people disappear.
claims.rests: He names no source in this line. The figure matches the Express, which says the revision struck more than 13 crore names off the draft rolls.
claims.site: The site's own sum across the 31 states and union territories with a draft is 13,39,03,307 names left off. In the states that published a full split by reason, about a fifth were entered as dead. In several states the final roll is larger than the draft.
claims.stops: The 13 crore are names left off draft rolls before anything was put back, and they include the dead and the duplicates. The site cannot say how many of them were eligible electors.

claims.quote: पश्चिम बंगाल में 27 लाख वोटरों को चुनाव में वोट देने का मौका नहीं मिला।
claims.translation: In West Bengal, 27 lakh voters did not get the chance to vote in the election.
claims.rests: This matches the state totals as reported. Of the 60,06,675 names held for adjudication, 27,16,393 were found not eligible.
claims.site: The West Bengal page also gives 32,68,119 found eligible and 37,05,235 appeals pending, as reported. Only 1,607 names were restored before the poll.
claims.stops: These are state totals as reported. With most appeals still pending, the site cannot say how many of the 27 lakh were eligible.

claims.quote: 20 अगस्त से 24 सितंबर के बीच 29,000 से ज्यादा फॉर्म सेवन भरे गए हैं। इनमें से 93% आम लोगों ने भरे हैं।
claims.translation: Between 20 August and 24 September more than 29,000 Form 7s were filed [in Karnataka], 93% of them by ordinary people.
claims.rests: He gives these as the figures of Rizwan Arshad, a Karnataka minister, from the minister's letter to the Chief Electoral Officer.
claims.site: The Disputes page lists the bulk Form 7 objections reported in Karnataka, each with its source. Karnataka's own pages carry the Chief Electoral Officer's district figures only.
claims.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no count of Form 7s by who filed them, so the 93 per cent cannot be set against an official figure.

claims.quote: नए वोटर और बहुत से पुराने वोटर के लिए इसका प्रमाण देना मुश्किल होने लगा और उनका नाम वोटर लिस्ट से कटने लगा।
claims.translation: For new voters and many old ones, proving this became difficult and their names began to be struck off the roll.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on the rolls
claims.rests: Form 6 is the application for new enrolment. The declaration could delay or block an application, and the Express says applicants could not submit without answering it. No source found shows it removing names already on the roll.
claims.site: The section on Form 6 on the process page sets out the declaration and the Commissioners' objections.
claims.stops: No count exists of Form 6 applications refused because of the declaration.

strongest: He follows the Express documents closely, and the figures he relays from them are right as reported.
The West Bengal adjudication figure he uses, 27 lakh, is the reported official one.
He relays a Bombay High Court bench's remarks on Goa, which are about process and can be checked.
further: He moves from the paper's findings about process to vote theft, which the paper itself does not claim.
He treats the 13 crore names left off the drafts as people erased.

people.name: Yogendra Yadav
people.role: Psephologist and political activist. He is one of the petitioners in the Supreme Court challenge to the Bihar revision and made submissions in person. He was with Lokniti at CSDS, is the founding national president of Swaraj India, a registered party, and convenes Bharat Jodo Abhiyan.
people.intro: His main method sets the roll against the projected adult population, which catches the young adults a count of deletions cannot see. The quotations are from reports of his submissions in court and of his talks.

pieces.title: 'Bihar SIR Is Intensive Deletion Exercise' : Yogendra Yadav Appears In Supreme Court With Two Persons Deleted As Dead By ECI
pieces.outlet: LiveLaw (Debby Jain), report of his oral submissions

pieces.title: Bihar SIR: 20 Lakh First-Time Voters Are Missing From Bihar's Draft Electoral Roll
pieces.outlet: The Wire (Pavan Korada; Yadav's calculation as told to The Wire)

pieces.title: Bihar SIR Key Takeaways: 'Missing Voters' Triple, Gender Skew Worse, 5 Lakh Voters With Gibberish Values
pieces.outlet: The Wire Staff, report of his presentation to the Supreme Court on 9 Oct 2025

pieces.title: BJP Using SIR To Cut Electorate In Opposition-Ruled States, Claims Yogendra Yadav
pieces.outlet: ETV Bharat (also carried by The Week as PTI copy)

claims.quote: a good electoral roll of Bihar should have 8 crore 18 lakh people, but it had 7.9 crores. So there was deficit of 29 lakhs to begin with
claims.rests: His oral submission in the Supreme Court, as LiveLaw reported it.
claims.site: The site uses the same kind of projection. It puts Bihar's adults at about 8.30 crore on 1 March 2026, against 7.90 crore on the roll before the revision and 7.24 crore on the draft. Across 19 states the rolls held 98.3 per cent of projected adults before the revision and 84.4 per cent on the drafts.
claims.stops: A projection counts residents. In a state that sends workers elsewhere it counts adults who may be registered where they came from, and the site says so beside the figure.

claims.quote: Total eligible adults: The government report projects Bihar's 18+ population in July 2025 at 8.18 crore ... New registered voters: The ECI's press release states that the new draft roll contains only 7.24 crore voters. The shortfall: 8.18 crore – 7.24 crore = 94 lakh.
claims.rests: His calculation as The Wire set it out. The arithmetic holds, and the ratio of electors to adults falls from 97 to 88 per cent.
claims.site: The site's figures move the same way. Bihar's draft held 7,24,05,756 names after 65,59,626 were left off in the first phase.
claims.stops: Part of the gap is young adults not yet enrolled and part is error in the projection, so the site does not call the whole of it disenfranchisement.

claims.quote: 25 lakh men and 31 lakh women have been deleted
claims.rests: His figures as LiveLaw reported them, with no source given. His reason, that more men migrate and die, is his own inference.
claims.site: The share matches the site's count closely, though the totals differ. The first-phase lists hold 36,39,976 women and 29,19,433 men, so women are 55.5 per cent of the names against 47.9 per cent of the roll. They are over-represented in all 38 districts and in 242 of 243 seats.
claims.stops: The lists do not say why. Moves on marriage account for about half a year's worth of the excess, and the district pattern runs against that explanation.

claims.quote: Never in the history of this country has any revision ever asked all people to submit a form or to submit a document. NEVER
claims.kind: A fact about how the revision was run
claims.rests: Said in reply to a question about 2003, when he asked the Commission to produce the 2003 order, which he said was not public.
claims.site: The process page sets out what the 2025 order asked of electors, from the order itself.
claims.stops: The site has not compared the 2003 instructions.

claims.quote: We are witnessing perhaps the largest exercise of disenfranchisement, not in India, in the history of the world. Entire figure will cross 1 crore, if they are serious about what they are doing.
claims.rests: A forecast made in August 2025.
claims.site: The final roll did not bear the forecast out as stated. After the draft 3,66,742 more names were removed and 21,53,343 added, and the final roll of 7,41,92,357 was 47,72,808 below the roll before the revision.
claims.stops: Disenfranchisement turns on who was eligible, and the lists record only the reason an officer wrote down.

claims.quote: From 27 lakh after the January 2025 special summary revision, the number of adults who are not registered as voters has gone up to 81 lakh in the SIR.
claims.rests: The Wire's account of his presentation to the Court. The article does not give his adult base, and 81 lakh plus the final roll implies about 8.23 crore.
claims.site: The same method on the site's projection of 8.30 crore gives about 88 lakh adults off the final roll.
claims.stops: As before, the projection counts residents.

claims.quote: From the outset, I have said SIR is targeted at Bengal. As Bihar elections were only a few months away, the EC used the state as the testing ground to implement SIR. Now the BJP wants to go the whole hog in Bengal
claims.outlet: PTI, as carried by ETV Bharat
claims.rests: A statement of purpose made at a public meeting in Kolkata, as PTI reported it.
claims.site: Nothing on the site measures purpose.
claims.stops: The site makes no claim about what anyone intended.

strongest: He measures the roll against the adult population, which catches young adults that a count of deletions cannot.
He pointed out early that more women than men were removed in Bihar, and the site's count of the lists bears it out in every district.
He raised problems in the final Bihar roll, entries with junk values and apparent duplicates, that can be checked against the roll.
further: Calling it the largest disenfranchisement in the history of the world, and saying it would cross 1 crore, were forecasts. Bihar's final roll fell by about 48 lakh.
He attributes a purpose to the BJP and the Commission from the choice of states alone.

people.name: Debraj Ray
people.role: Economist at New York University, writing as an individual in a research note on his own site.
people.intro: His note of 10 May 2026 asks whether West Bengal's deletions could account for the BJP's majority, and shows how the answer moves with each assumption.

pieces.title: SIR and the BJP's Bengal Majority

claims.quote: If we restrict ourselves to the adjudicated SIR deletions, and even if we make the incredibly heroic assumption that every deleted voter would have obediently turned out, and that every such voter would have voted for the runner-up ... that flips a maximum of 26 ACs away from the BJP. The resulting number, 207-26 =181, leaves the BJP comfortably above the 148-seat majority threshold
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: An upper bound under assumptions he states. It agrees with Newslaundry's count and with The Wire's, which reached 25.
claims.site: His state totals come from the same press note the site uses. They give 7,66,37,529 electors before the revision, 58,20,899 left off the draft, 60,06,675 held for adjudication and 27,16,393 found not eligible.
claims.stops: The Chief Electoral Officer has published no adjudication outcomes by constituency, so the site does not compute this bound.

claims.quote: Under any neutral calibration, the BJP retains majority by more than thirty seats. The deletions hypothesis only reverses this result at extreme calibrations that the data refuse to support
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: His widest bound, which counts the shifted and absent as well, flips 69 seats and leaves the BJP ten short of a majority. He argues it would need about 92 per cent turnout among the removed and about 95 per cent of them voting against the BJP.
claims.site: The site's Bihar estimate works the same way. In 187 of 243 seats the runner-up could not have won even with every removed elector's vote, and the estimates have 4 to 6 seats changing hands in both directions.
claims.stops: No one knows how the removed would have voted. Where the site cannot assume it, it gives the share of votes the runner-up would have needed.

claims.quote: BJP MLAs were associated with more adjudicated deletions in their own seats, about 15 more per thousand voters ... It is consistent with the strategic-targeting story for the adjudication channel ... But the offsetting movement in non-adjudicated deletions along the same dimensions means that the overall contestable rate ... shows no partisan-targeting signal.
claims.rests: His strongest evidence of a partisan pattern. He calls it a correlation and states its limit in the same passage.
claims.site: The site measures the fall in the roll, a different count. Set against their own districts, seats the AITC won lost 0.23 more per 100 and seats the BJP won 0.03 more.
claims.stops: The site holds no adjudication figures by seat, so it cannot test his finding directly.

claims.quote: This is not an argument that the SIR did not matter. It clearly mattered in particular constituencies ... Why individuals had to be put through this ordeal in this particular election, with many plausibly denied their constitutional rights, is a question that should hold our attention.

strongest: He states every assumption and shows how the answer changes with it.
He separates the deletions decided in adjudication, where a partisan pattern appears, from those made by booth-level officers, where none does.
further: He sets aside the 24.2 lakh entered as dead as removals that can be defended. In Bihar the site found deaths entered at about 3.4 years' worth, with women over-represented, so a death on the list is what the officer wrote down, and nobody checked it.

people.name: Newslaundry
people.role: Independent news site funded by its subscribers. The analysis is by Samarth Grover.
people.intro: Its piece of 7 May 2026 runs four tests of rising strictness on West Bengal's deletions and reports how the answer shrinks.

pieces.title: 4 tests, 1 question: Did SIR shape Bengal outcome?

claims.quote: If we compare the 2026 winning margins to the net deletions in each constituency, we get 82 BJP-won constituencies where deletions exceeded the party's victory margin. Of these, 70 were seats that flipped from TMC to BJP.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: A count of seats where deletions exceeded the margin, which the author calls the point where the data starts to raise questions.
claims.site: Measured by the fall in the roll from 2024, the site finds the fall larger than the margin in 139 of 294 seats, taking every party together.
claims.stops: A count larger than the margin measures size. It cannot show an effect.

claims.quote: An even stricter test, comparing UA deletions to the electoral swing from 2021, shows that in 14 seats, the deletions were higher than the overall change in margin. Of these 14, the BJP won only one – Pandabeswar – and the TMC won the rest in 2026.
claims.kind: A reading of the effect on results
claims.rests: As published. The article adds that the TMC had won all 14 in 2021.
claims.site: The site has not run this test.
claims.stops: The site holds no deletions under adjudication by seat.

claims.quote: The assumption most commonly made – that the deleted voters were TMC's – deserves particular scepticism ... Both things can be true simultaneously: a revision can be administratively legitimate and electorally consequential

Whether that overlap reflects correction, disenfranchisement, or some combination of both may remain unresolved. That is a question of public interest that warrants a full and transparent answer, something which the Election Commission refuses to provide.
claims.rests: The article's closing paragraph.
claims.site: The site's figures stop at the same place.
claims.stops: The lists cannot tell a correction from a wrongful removal, and the Commission has not published what would.

strongest: Four tests, each stated, with the answer shrinking from 82 seats to one, and an explicit refusal to claim a cause.
further: Very little. It calls the measure based on adjudication more targeted, which describes the measure and says nothing of intent.

people.name: Lokniti-CSDS
people.role: The survey programme of the Centre for the Study of Developing Societies, Delhi. The report quoted is The Wire's, by Pavan Korada.
people.intro: Its survey of August 2025, 3,054 interviews in five states and Delhi, asked who holds the documents the Commission's order listed.

pieces.title: 'SIR Risks Disenfranchising Millions of Legitimate Citizens Over Lack of Documents': Lokniti-CSDS Survey

claims.quote: A majority of respondents, 52%, do not have a birth certificate. Furthermore, 41% lack a domicile certificate and 42% do not possess a caste certificate.
claims.rests: Survey figures as The Wire reported them.
claims.site: The site has no survey of documents.
claims.stops: Lacking a document did not by itself remove anyone. In the later phases most electors were matched to the 2002 to 2005 rolls and asked for no document, and Aadhaar was later accepted on the Supreme Court's orders.

claims.quote: three-quarters of the citizens who have none of the required documents belong to the lower half of the economic order.
claims.rests: As The Wire reported it.
claims.site: The site does not measure household income. Its All India comparisons use each state's income per head.
claims.stops: The site cannot say who among the removed held which document.

claims.quote: the current requirements could pose a 'serious challenge for many of those who have a legitimate right to be part of the voters' list.'
claims.rests: A statement of risk, hedged in the report's own words.

strongest: It is the only independent survey of who holds the documents the order listed, and it hedges its own conclusion.
further: The Wire's headline, that the revision risks disenfranchising millions, is stronger than the survey's own wording.
